- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model underestimates; apply upward bias correction.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope or add lagged mean reversion.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline after peak), model overreacts; dampen forecast trend.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture short-term sentiment-driven volatility; adjust forecast to align with sentiment volatility index (e.g., if sentiment >0.7, allow 2–3% upward adjustment; if <0.3, allow 2–3% downward).
- If model forecast is flat or rising slowly while sentiment is rising sharply, model underestimates momentum; increase forecast slope by 1–2% per sentiment unit above 0.5.
- If model forecast is rising rapidly while sentiment is falling, model overestimates; reduce forecast slope by 1–2% per sentiment unit below 0.5.
